claim: Adding a hard IsValid() gate to the previously-lenient CommandResponseFromJSON parser turns tolerated integration payloads (e.g. an unrecognized response_type such as "comment") into hard failures: an outgoing slash-command response now surfaces to the user as a 500 via app/command.go:595-596, discarding text/attachments/goto_location/props that were previously delivered; /hooks/commands returns 400; and Client4.ExecuteCommand can no longer decode a server/plugin response with a non-standard response_type. The all-or-nothing recursion over ExtraResponses (lines 90-98) defeats HandleCommandResponse's per-entry partial-delivery design — one bad nested entry discards the whole valid main response.
raw: #1 🟠 High: Previously-tolerated slash-command responses now fail the whole execution, and one bad `extra_responses` entry discards the valid main response

claim: maxLength := 65535 is a hardcoded byte count while the real downstream post limit is a runtime rune count from determineMaxPostSize that scales with an enlarged Posts.Message column, so installations with an enlarged column can have previously-postable responses rejected; in the default config the check is also too loose (16383-rune limit vs 65535 bytes) so it does not shield the caller from post-creation failure; and it duplicates the existing PostMessageMaxBytesV2 constant as an unnamed local.
raw: #3 🟡 Medium: Hardcoded 65535-*byte* text cap ignores the configurable post size and can reject responses that previously posted fine

claim: Validation was added to CommandResponseFromJSON rather than CommandResponseFromHTTPBody, so the text/plain branch (CommandResponseFromPlainText) bypasses IsValid entirely — the same oversized text is rejected as JSON but accepted as plain text on both ingress paths (web/webhook.go:114 and app/command.go:586,595), so the cap does not achieve its stated bound.
